scope: Labelled hypotheses for January calendar names without a local source; reviewed history for Mundrīte; check of an external system answer.

external_check.name: Mundrīte
external_check.summary: An external AI answer (pasted by the user) correctly linked Mundrīte with Mundra and the adjective mundrs and cited Siliņš 1990 p. 244, matching our data. It missed that Mundra is recorded in Saldus in 1931 and has been in the calendar since 1921. Unverified or wrong parts: bearer counts (about 2 and 10), the site personvardi.lu.lv, an invented interwar origin scenario, and “Traugots” given as a Baltic name (it is German Traugott). Use such answers only as pointers to sources.

method: As round 136 (template write-r136.mjs; build-r139.mjs = helpers + r139-data.mjs). Names with a root history, an existing hypothesis or a reviewed history were skipped. Wording follows the 16 November rule: no sources and no Russian origin in the text. Latvian/Lithuanian word template now uses “Vārds/Vardas X …” (gender-neutral); round 136 rebuilt with it.
